Background (from the session that started this one):
AGENTS.md says wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer, and that `wording.test.ts` guards this. The test and `OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp` last changed in commit faa5fbd32f ("Stop naming Orca to the model, and keep each request sent to it"). The failure was seen while another session was changing the printer and filament chat message boxes, and that uncommitted work does not touch either file. Other sessions share this checkout, so touch only the files this task needs and do not stash, reset or switch branches.

Task:
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts`, the test "never names Orca in what the app writes for the model", fails on `jusprin-newui`. It flags the literals "Orca Slicer", "OrcaSlicer" and "Orca" in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp`. Find out whether each literal reaches the model. If it does, change the wording so the model reads "the app". If it does not, narrow the test so it stays strict for text the model reads. Done means `npx vitest run` passes in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`, and you have shown the guard still fails when a real model-facing string names Orca. Do not commit unless Kenneth asks.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_d15e9191-9376-400d-acf9-504c5a5d4808

faa5fbd32f Stop naming Orca to the model, and keep each request sent to it
A reply on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash said "Orca did flag two things", as if a second
program were involved. The saved chat could not show why, because the app kept
no record of what it sent. This commit makes four changes.

Rebrand the bare word in the catalogs: brand_catalogs.py now turns "Orca" on
its own into the product name, so warnings such as "Orca will automatically
cap the jerk" reach the person and the model as JusPrin. Names such as Orca
Cloud and Orca Cube keep their wording.

Reword what the app writes for the model: tool descriptions, tool results,
notes and skills say "the app". wording.test.ts fails if the name returns, and
AGENTS.md states the rule. Only the prompt still names OrcaSlicer, to explain
that file data using the name means this app.

Rename the product in setting tooltips: the settings tools send a tooltip's
source text, which skips the catalogs, so 13 settings still said "Orca Slicer"
or "Orca" to the model. setting_definition now replaces the name with the
product name, the word the person already sees in the same tooltip.
PrintConfig.cpp is unchanged. A new test reads every setting's text; it failed
on those 13 before this change.

Keep the requests: each request is written to
<data dir>/jusprin/request-log as one JSON file, the newest 200. A picture or
file becomes a note of its size. Headers stay out, so the file holds no API
key. Responses and the model's reasoning are not logged. A file that cannot be
written costs the log only, and the request still goes out.

Tested with agent_bridge_tests, setting_display_tests,
workspace_contract_tests, jusprin_tests, test_brand_catalogs.py,
wording.test.ts and the prompt runner's offline tests. In the shell harness,
one chat message went through the app's own agent to a fake local provider and
the logged body equalled the body received, and settings_search returned the
new tooltip wording with no Orca in the reply. tests/project_prompt/baseline.json
still holds the old tools hash and needs a live recording.

#!/bin/bash
# Injects a violation, runs the Orca wording guard, restores the file byte for byte
# with its mtime, so a later build sees no change.
R=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin

DEFS=$R/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp
REG=$R/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp
BK=$(dirname "$0")/backup
mkdir -p "$BK"

probe() { # name file perl-expression
  local name=$1 file=$2 expr=$3 copy="$BK/$(basename "$file")"
  cp -p "$file" "$copy"
  perl -0pi -e "$expr" "$file"
  if cmp -s "$file" "$copy"; then echo "=== $name: INJECTION DID NOT APPLY"; return; fi

  (cd "$UI" && npx vitest run src/wording.test.ts -t "never names Orca" 2>&1) \
    | grep -E '^\+ +"|Tests +|No test' | sed "s|$R/||"
  cp -p "$copy" "$file"
  cmp "$file" "$copy" && echo "restored"
}

content.text:
The test "never names Orca in what the app writes for the model" passes again, and `npx vitest run` in `AgentUI` passes all 624 tests. The three flagged names never reach the model, so I narrowed the test and changed no C++. Only [wording.test.ts](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts) changed, and nothing is committed.

## Why the names don't reach the model
- **What the code does:** all three names are on one line, [OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp:43](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp:43). They are the search terms `with_product_name` passes to `replace_all`, which swaps each one for the product name in a tooltip. `name` is used nowhere else.
- **Runtime check:** the already-built C++ test "No setting names Orca in what the model reads" passes (1307 assertions). That binary was built after the header's last change.
- **How long it has failed:** that line and the guard both arrived in commit faa5fbd32f, so the guard has probably failed since then, even though the commit message lists `wording.test.ts` as tested. I inferred this from the file contents and did not run the test at that commit.

## The change
The guard now removes that exact `for` line and its `replace_all` body from the header text before scanning. If either line changes, the exemption stops matching and the guard reads the names again.

## Proof the guard still fails
I injected each violation into the real source file, ran the guard, then restored the file:

| Injected violation | Guard result |
|---|---|
| A real tool description in `ToolRegistry.cpp` says "Orca validates…" | Fails |
| The same header appends " Orca will cap it." to a tooltip | Fails, flagging only that string |
| The loop's list gains "Orca Cloud" | Fails |
| The loop body becomes `text += name;`, which would send the names to the model | Fails |
| No injection | Passes |

## A mistake during testing
My first probe script had a bug that made no usable backups, so the injected violations stayed in `ToolRegistry.cpp` and `OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp` for about a minute around 05:12–05:13. I restored both files, then reran the probes with a fixed script; the table shows that rerun.

- **Current state:** `git status` shows neither file as modified, and both have their original timestamps, so they won't trigger a rebuild. The header's timestamp is only accurate to the minute.
- **Possible effect on other sessions:** no build was running when I checked just before the probes and just after restoring. A `vitest` run by another session in that minute could have seen a false failure in this test.
